nodes.title: USAID contracting-officer bribery involving Apprio and Vistant

legal_status_as_reported.description: DOJ reported individual guilty pleas and corporate deferred prosecution agreements with admissions. OIG later reported individual debarment notices dated August 26, 2025.
legal_status_as_reported.not_claimed: No representation of present debarment eligibility, final sentencing outcomes, or subsequent appeals or modifications.

mechanism.summary: Existing contractors bribed a contracting officer; prime and subcontract roles changed. A subcontractor intermediary, false payroll transfers, shell entities and false invoices concealed benefits. The officer influenced awards, disclosed procurement information, supplied favorable evaluations and approved contract decisions.

source_reported_evidence.description: OIG says an allegation of disclosure of bid, proposal or source-selection information triggered its investigation. It reports May 2025 guilty pleas, referral to the suspension and debarment official, and subsequent debarment notices.

DOJ attributes its mechanism account to court documents and reports guilty pleas, corporate admissions and cooperation. It names FBI, USAID OIG and IRS Criminal Investigation as investigators. The release describes transfers and concealment, but this review has not examined the underlying account records or exhibits.

amount_interpretation.description: DOJ's over $550 million concerns contract volume, not established loss or a per-unit premium. Its approximately $1 million-plus bribe amount is expressly alleged. Neither figure calibrates a 12 percent markup.

researcher_inferences: Matching a legal name, CAGE and UEI tests identity consistency; it does not test buyer independence or the absence of corrupt benefits.
An arithmetically correct award amount can coexist with a corrupt award decision; arithmetic alone is not a fair-price test.
Reported offer counts do not show who prepared each bid, whether offers were independently determined, the price spread, or whether confidential information was leaked.

A useful next record is the contemporaneous bid and evaluation trail linked to the decisionmaker's role dates. Payment or benefit tracing requires actual supporting records, not an inferred connection from price alone.
transfer_limitations: This services-procurement case supplies a corruption mechanism, not a market-price comparator for DLA machine bolts.
No evidence in these sources links these case participants or mechanisms to the studied DLA bolt awards.
No recurring percentage, independent comparable unit price, invoice-level loss, or buyer kickback is established for the DLA cohort.
A premium can reflect ordinary margin, quantity, specification, timing, freight, risk, or a poor purchase; establishing an unexplained premium and establishing bribery are separate evidentiary tasks.

protocol.name: Amount-weighted premium
protocol.test: For a single declared amount basis, compute E=sum(q*(p-b)), B=sum(q*b), A=sum(q*p); weighted_markup=E/B and excess_share_of_gross=E/A. Require B>0, A>0, finite numbers and common currency.
protocol.output: signed excess, positive-only difference separately, baseline-weighted percentage, amount coverage and uncertainty interval
protocol.guard: Do not average percentages equally or drop negative differences; no mixed ordered/invoiced/paid rows.

protocol.name: Repeated 12 percent hypothesis
protocol.test: Before reading outcomes, declare 0.12 as a hypothesis, tolerance (for example 0.01), minimum independent solicitations/periods and complete eligible universe. Count rows and baseline-weighted amount within the band, report all residuals and benchmark sensitivity. Split exploratory and held-out periods; do not round values into a 12 percent pattern.
protocol.output: observed repetition and coverage, not a kickback probability
protocol.guard: Thresholds are analyst-selected screening settings, not official fraud cutoffs. Multiple lines under one solicitation are not independent repetitions. Seven incomplete history rows cannot establish this test.

protocol.guard: Do not impose a generic inflation series or assume retail availability at a government delivery date. No regression on eight incomparable records.

properties.framework_origin: Research design informed by the cited official methodology and known-case mechanisms
normalization_rules: Require documented pack and price units. Dividing box price by a claimed per-piece display can check arithmetic but cannot prove pack count.
Keep item price and government-paid freight distinct, then compare like landed-cost bases. FOB origin does not mean free shipping.
Use quantities actually ordered/invoiced/paid for the chosen basis; an annual estimate, ceiling or cancelled balance is not volume purchased.
Require actual revision/grade/thread/finish/traceability equivalence or a documented technical adjustment; do not use ASME B18.24 alone as a complete product specification.
Preserve the source's monetary precision and round only at declared reporting stages; do not select a tier whose minimum order exceeds feasible demand without accounting for all packs purchased.
Do not infer dated availability from today's stock, or a historical comparable from a current page. Preserve quote validity and delivery capacity.

Maintain business identity and beneficial ownership as different relations. A current CAGE/UEI match, self-parent record, shared upstream manufacturer or punctuation alias does not prove historical ownership or bid coordination.
Do not merge awards, invoice lines and cash disbursements; use unique parent/order/modification/CLIN keys and deduplicate cumulative obligations.
